summary: Registers the application/pkix-attr-cert MIME media type, used to carry a single attribute certificate as defined in RFC 5755. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC registers a media type for transferring a single attribute certificate. The type gives MIME-based applications a label for the binary content.

subtitle: Registers a MIME media type for carrying one attribute certificate.

tldr.problem: Attribute certificates needed a MIME media type for transfer, alongside the types RFC 2585 defines for public key certificates and revocation lists.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers application/pkix-attr-cert for a single attribute certificate defined in RFC 5755.
tldr.outcome: The registered type uses binary encoding and has no required or optional parameters.

today: RFC 5877 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: A Media Type for Attribute Certificates
sections.content:
RFC 2585 defines MIME media types for public key certificates and certificate revocation lists. RFC 5877 specifies the media type application/pkix-attr-cert for an attribute certificate defined in RFC 5755.

Attribute certificates use ASN.1 encoding. RFC 5755 specifies which parts use DER and which may use BER; DER is a subset of BER.
sections.plainLanguage: The new media type labels content that carries one attribute certificate. The certificate itself is encoded using ASN.1 rules.

sections.title: The Media Type Registration
sections.content:
The type is application and its subtype is pkix-attr-cert. It has no required or optional parameters, uses binary encoding, and has the file extension .ac. The registration lists no magic number and names RFC 5755 as the published specification.

The type is intended for MIME-compliant transports, including HTTP use to fetch attribute certificates. The RFC says other uses may emerge.
sections.plainLanguage: The registered label is application/pkix-attr-cert. It identifies binary content and has no parameters.

sections.title: Matching Certificate Names
sections.content:
An attribute certificate provides authorization information and is often used with a public key certificate. The issuer must encode the holder entity name in exactly the same way as the distinguished name in the public key certificate.

If the names are encoded differently, an implementation may fail to recognize that the two certificates belong to the same entity.
sections.plainLanguage: The name must use the same encoding in both certificates. Otherwise, software may not connect them to the same entity.
